reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of EMH is that betting odds already reflect all available information, so converting them to probabilities must respect this. The OO-EPC primitive assumes that bet volume scales linearly with inverse odds, allowing estimation of true probabilities through a variance-adjusted inverse transformation. It avoids overfitting by using only the structure of odds themselves, not historical outcomes. The FL-GLM extends this by modeling the systematic bias in odds—particularly favoritism and longshot bias—via a single parameter β. This allows for a more nuanced correction than simple normalization. Both primitives are robust under EMH because they do not attempt to recover information already embedded in the odds. Instead, they refine the interpretation of those odds to better approximate true event probabilities. The failure mode of OO-EPC occurs when the assumed variance structure breaks down, triggering fallback behavior. FL-GLM fails when β deviates significantly from observed patterns, indicating misalignment between model assumptions and market dynamics.
